analysis.title: On Our Minds: October CPI: Another Upside Surprise
key_insights: October core CPI rose 0.3% m/m (0.296% unrounded), above the 0.2% consensus and in line with the SG forecast of 0.3%. Estimated y/y is 2.8% vs 2.6% in September.

Headline CPI rose 0.4% m/m vs a consensus and SG expectation of 0.3%, after +0.6% in September. SG estimates y/y at 4.1% vs 3.7% in September. The BLS did not publish a y/y figure because of data issues tied to the 2025 government shutdown, so this is SG's interpolation from the NSA October 2025 number.
Energy CPI rose 0.7% m/m after +5.2% in September. Gasoline rose 1% m/m after +9.1%. Food CPI rose 0.5% m/m after being essentially flat in September.
Shelter rose 0.3% m/m vs 0.4% in September. CPI OER (0.3% m/m) and rent of primary residence (0.2% m/m) matched September's pace.

CPI core goods rose 0.2% m/m vs 0.3% in September, held down by used vehicles (-1.2% m/m). Excluding vehicles, core goods rose 0.5% m/m after +0.2%, with medical commodities accelerating meaningfully.
Non-housing core services CPI (super-core CPI) rose 0.4% m/m vs 0.3% in September. Medical care and transportation services were the main drivers.
SG's direct estimate for PCE housing in October is 0.28% m/m, a small step down from 0.32% in September. PCE core goods is estimated at 0.25% m/m vs 0.20% in September.

Housing (~18% weight) and core goods (~24% weight) cover less than half of core PCE, so the October core PCE forecast depends mostly on super-core PCE. Most of its source data comes from the PPI release, so the CPI gives no information on it.

If monthly super-core PCE reverts to its six-month average (0.28% m/m), core PCE comes in near 0.27%. If it stays near the August-September pace (0.37% m/m), core PCE is near 0.32%. SG's central estimate is about 0.30% m/m (range 0.27%-0.33%) pending the October PPI.

macro_indicators.interpretation: Upside surprise vs expectations, but slower than September's 0.6%. Food and energy were the contributors.
